jobs.occupation: First Research Article Fellowship Program (Forschungsreferent/in)
jobs.description:
First Research Article Fellowship Program at the Max Planck Institute for the History

of Science, Berlin

01 September 2027 – 28 February 2028

The Max Planck Institute for the History of Science ( MPIWG) is offering six-month

fellowships for outstanding graduate students enrolled in doctoral programs based at

Asian, African, or Latin American institutions.

Applicants should demonstrate their commitment to a research topic related to the history of

science, technology, and medicine, or science and technology studies, and a need to work

with an international community at the MPIWG in order to prepare and publish their first

single-authored research paper in English.

First Research Article Fellows will be hosted in one of the following departments:

• Artefacts, Action, Knowledge (AAK – Director: Prof. Dr. Dagmar Schäfer)

• Knowledge Systems and Collective Life (KSCL – Director: Prof. Dr. Etienne Benson)

Regular meetings will be held to support both the writing process and academic

development. Fellows are welcome and encouraged to take part in activities offered by the

Institute and by the International Max Planck Research School “Knowledge and Its

Resources” that take place on our campus.

Candidates are expected to have already completed the relevant research for their thesis and

be in a position to devote six months to writing and preparing an article in English for

journal publication. Fellows must remain enrolled in their home institution’s doctoral

program through the end of the advertised fellowship period.

Fellowships are endowed with a monthly stipend according to the guidelines of the Max

Planck Society (https://www.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/research/projects/first-research-article-

fellowship).

Applicants should submit the following materials in English through our online application

portal:

1. Cover letter explaining how the applicant’s proposed research fits the research

themes of one specific department

1. Official enrollment certificate and confirmation that the applicant will remain

enrolled in an accredited graduate program (PhD) through the end of the

fellowship

1. 500-word description of the dissertation written by the applicant
2. Curriculum vitae (preferably without a photograph) including any publications if

applicable

1. Title, abstract, and outline of article to be completed during the fellowship

(maximum 750 words)

1. English-language writing sample (maximum 8000 words including notes and

bibliography) written by the applicant7. A letter of recommendation from one supervisor

This program is intended to support scholars who wish to improve their academic English.

We encourage you to write your application without the use of AI.

The Max Planck Institute for the History of Science encourages applications from qualified

individuals who belong to groups that are often underrepresented in the workplace due to age,

disability, ethnicity, family status, gender, nationality, race, sex, sexual orientation,

socioeconomic background, or religion.

Please note that only electronic submissions will be accepted. Applications must be

uploaded to the following link on or before 15 January 2027 (23:59 CET):

https://recruitment.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/position/36470793

Finalists may expect a decision by 1 April 2027.

Descriptions of the research projects undertaken by the departments can be found here:

Artifacts, Action, Knowledge (AAK):

https://www.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/research/department/artifacts-action-knowledge

Knowledge Systems and Collective Life (KSCL):

https://www.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/research/department/knowledge-systems-collective-life

For further information, please consult the Frequently Asked Questions at the program’s

website: https://www.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/research/projects/first-research-article-

fellowship.

For all other questions, contact the Publications Manager for this program, Lindy

Divarci                 divarci@mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de

Max Planck Institute for the History of Science

Boltzmannstr. 22, 14195 Berlin

jobs.occupation: Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d) (Physiker/in)
jobs.employer_name: Max-Planck-Gesellschaft zur Förderung der Wissenschaft e.V Max-Planck-Institut für Physik
jobs.description:
Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d)

The Semiconductor Laboratory (HLL) of the Max Planck Society, located on the research campus in Garching near Munich, is a leading facility for the development of highly precise radiation sensors and detector systems. On approximately 1,400 m² of cleanroom space, HLL develops, fabricates and tests advanced semiconductor detectors for applications in X-ray astronomy, particle physics and materials research. With around 50 employees from different nationalities, HLL provides a highly international and interdisciplinary environment in which scientists, engineers and technology specialists work closely together across the entire development chain — from fundamental research and simulation to device design, fabrication and experimental characterization.

To strengthen our activities in quantum sensing and advanced quantum-device technologies, and to provide scientific and technological support to our research, engineering and service teams, we are looking for a Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d) to join our team at the earliest possible date on a full-time basis (39 hours/week). 

Your responsibilities

- Develop and optimize quantum sensor concepts based on qubit systems and quantum effects.
- Perform advanced numerical simulations and modeling of qubit-based sensing systems, including relevant physical processes, noise sources and system-level performance.
- Work closely with technology development, engineering and experimental teams to translate simulation results into practical implementations.
- Analyze experimental data and use the results to refine physical models and sensor designs.
- Contribute to scientific publications, technical documentation and intellectual property.

Your profile

- PhD in physics, electrical engineering, applied physics, quantum engineering or a related field.
- Background in quantum sensing, qubit control and precision measurement.
- Experience with numerical simulation, modeling and system design.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills combined with a practical, technology-oriented mindset.
- Strong motivation to work in close cooperation with technology, engineering and experimental teams.
- Fluency in English; knowledge of German is an advantage.

Advantageous experience

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be particularly valuable:

- Cleanroom / semiconductor / microfabrication experience
- Familiarity with Python, MATLAB, COMSOL or equivalent 
- MEMS/NEMS or integrated sensor technologies
- Precision measurement and low-noise instrumentation
- Experience bridging qubit physics, device design and fabrication technology

What we offer

- International environment, diverse responsibilities and a high degree of autonomy: Flat hierarchies and a collaborative, agile team within an internationally renowned research institution. jobs.occupation: BTA, MTA oder CTA (m/f/d) – CG-2026-2 (Biologisch-technische/r Assistent/in)
jobs.description:
The LIT - Leibniz Institute for Immunotherapy (foundation under civil law) (https://lit.eu/) – is a biomedical research center focusing on translational immunology in the fields of cancer immunotherapy, transplant rejection and autoimmunity. The objective of the LIT is to develop innovative and efficient cellular immune therapeutics in these areas. Our own GMP laboratories and close networking with University and University Hospital offer excellent opportunities for clinical translation of novel immune cell products.

The Flow Cytometry Core Facility is recruiting a highly motivated

BTA, MTA oder CTA (m/f/d) – CG-2026-2

(full time, 40.1 hours per week)

The position is initially limited to two years with the possibility of extension.

The Flow Cytometric Cell Analytics and Cell Sorting Core Facility at the LIT offers research groups from the LIT, the University Hospital of Regensburg (UKR), and the University of Regensburg (UR) the opportunity to identify and characterize individual cell populations and to isolate them in a targeted manner, thus making them accessible for further downstream analysis. In addition, the facility offers advice and support for beginners and advanced users on flow cytometry-related questions and problems, such as the selection of appropriate fluorochromes, the creation of staining panels and the optimization of gating strategies.

We are now looking for a highly motivated technical assistant with excitement for flow cytometry, sophisticated instruments, organizational/administrative skills and a stong service mentality who is excited to enrich our facility. The facility hosts state-of-the art sorters and analyzers. The community of users is highly international and covers a range of scientific topics within and associated with Immunology.

Your tasks include, but are not limited to:

- Daily operation of the sorting machines
- Monitor and maintain the equipment in the facility, including arriving spectral cytometers. This includes quality control and cleaning of equipment.
- Reagent and consumables management, including planning, tracking and ordering of reagents and preparation of solutions and reagents
- Documentation, SOP and data management, including tracking and recording of instrument usage per user, creating and updating protocols for instruments, data backup and transfer to sorter users
- User support, including assisting users with scheduling of experiments, training experienced users for independent equipment usage of sorting machines and their software, expert advice to users
- Support for research initiatives of the facility, e.g. assisting flow cytometry-related research projects, assay development, promote the facility’s scientific work
- Management of facility waste, including autoclaving and coordination of waste disposal
- Ensure smooth operation of the facility

The ideal candidate possesses:

- Completed education as BTA, MTA or CTA
- Experience in handling of live cells, advanced equipment, flow cytometry
- High affinity for and ideally experience with work with sophisticated equipment, incuding equipment maintenance and trouble-shooting
- Experience in providing training
- Self-motivated person with an intrinsic service mentality, a collaborative attitude and the drive to advance the research within the institute
- Reliable and precise work style, high degree of independence
- Good organizational and administrative skills
- Good inter-personal skills, good communication skills in English and German
- Interest, and ideally also experience in working in an interdisciplinary and international environment

We offer:

- An international cutting-edge research environment that offers exciting and diverse opportunities
- Flat hierarchies and short decision-making processes
- A highly motivated and cooperative team
- Flexible working hours
- Job ticket and excellent benefits
- Excellent funding situation and state-of-the-art equipment

The remuneration is based on TV-L.

The Leibniz Institute for Immunotherapy aims to increase the share of women in the workforce. Therefore, qualified female candidates are explicitly encouraged to submit their applications. Moreover, the LIT advocates for the compatibility of family and career.

Disabled applicants (m/f/d) with equal qualifications will receive preferential treatment within the recruitment procedure. Please refer to your disability status already in your application.

Please note that expenses that may arise in the context of an eventual job interview cannot be reimbursed.

For more information, please contact Prof. Dr. Carmen Gerlach (carmen.gerlach@lit.eu). We are looking forward to receiving your detailed application in German or English. Please apply via our Online - Application Portal (https://rci.hr4you.org/job/view/113/bta-mta-oder-cta-m-f-d-cg-2026-2?page_lang=en) the reference CG- 2026-2.

Application deadline is October 11th 2026.
